/**
 * @name Unsafe deserialization with pickle
 * @description Using pickle to deserialize untrusted data can lead to arbitrary code execution
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/unsafe-deserialization-scipy
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-502
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  (
    call = API::moduleImport("pickle").getMember(["load", "loads", "Unpickler"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("_pickle").getMember(["load", "loads", "Unpickler"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("dill").getMember(["load", "loads"]).getACall() or
    call = API::moduleImport("joblib").getMember("load").getACall()
  )
select call, "Potentially unsafe deserialization operation that could execute arbitrary code if data is untrusted."
findings.hypothesis: Check for unsafe deserialization using pickle or similar modules that could lead to arbitrary code execution

findings.codeql_raw_query:
/**
 * @name Path traversal vulnerability
 * @description User-controlled paths used in file operations without validation can lead to unauthorized file access
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/path-traversal-scipy
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.RemoteFlowSources
import semmle.python.Concepts
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module PathTraversalConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    source instanceof RemoteFlowSource or
    exists(DataFlow::Node argv |
      argv = API::moduleImport("sys").getMember("argv").getAValueReachableFromSource() and
      source = argv
    )
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    sink = any(FileSystemAccess fa).getAPathArgument()
  }
}

module PathTraversalFlow = TaintTracking::Global<PathTraversalConfig>;
import PathTraversalFlow::PathGraph

from PathTraversalFlow::PathNode source, PathTraversalFlow::PathNode sink
where PathTraversalFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Potential path traversal from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Path traversal vulnerabilities where user-controlled paths are used in file operations without validation
